newhire_meera: Hi folks! First day here 🎉. I'm on an M2 MBA and trying to get the dev env running. Followed the onboarding (Homebrew + asdf) but some CLIs (pipx-installed tools, brew-installed ripgrep) aren't being found. My dotfiles are a little messy from previous jobs. Any recommended minimal zsh snippets for PATH and asdf init so I don't end up with system python/node first? Also: do people here use Rosetta for anything common?

jon: welcome Meera! Minimal bits I put in ~/.zprofile on macs: 
```bash
# Homebrew (Apple silicon)
export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/sbin:$PATH
# asdf (installed via brew)
. "$(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh" || true
# user-local (pipx, npm global) should be before fallback system bins
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```
That order puts asdf shims before /usr/bin. Rosetta only needed if you intentionally run intel-only binaries; we rarely require it.

devx_milo: +1. A few troubleshooting commands if things look off: `which -a python node pipx rg`, `asdf current`, `asdf reshim`, and `echo $PATH`. If you had pyenv/rbenv before, uninstall to avoid collisions. For pipx: install into the asdf python, not brew python: `python -m pip install --user pipx && pipx ensurepath` and then restart shell.

infra-bot: See onboarding snippet: <internal/dev-setup/macos-paths-asdf.md>. Reminder: add PATH/asdf init to ~/.zprofile on mac so GUI-launched apps (like Code started from dock) pick it up if you start VS Code from terminal with `code .` it's fine.

newhire_meera: thanks! quick Q: my existing dotfiles put PATH modifications in ~/.zshrc — is that problematic on mac?

jon: macOS treats shells as login shells; put PATH and asdf init in ~/.zprofile. Keep ~/.zshrc for interactive stuff (aliases, prompts) that runs every shell.

newhire_meera: ok moving them. One last thing: when I run `which -a python` I see /usr/bin/python3 first then /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 then the asdf shim. After moving lines to zprofile it updated to show the asdf shim first. Looks good. If I hit more weirdness I'll paste outputs. Thanks for the quick help! :)
